findings: The old portable collector accepted four independently resealed synthetic origin/profile/compiler/observer counterexamples; the v2 collector rejects them while retaining valid cross-VM collection after producer directories are removed.

Shared local and portable v2 validation checks the complete exact Cargo command, producer checkout source/manifest, selected target/profile/features, unique original compiler-artifact, final successful Cargo event, original/copy hash and size, compiler verbose identity, logs, configs and Git/loaded observer binding.

The active protocol observer preserves bytes before decoding, drains the entire normal EOF and rejects malformed UTF-8/JSON and unmatched/duplicate terminal replies. Declared SIGKILL can interrupt stdout and remains explicitly labeled.

Source-bound schema extraction supports both original manifest shapes, rejects ambiguous paths and validates the original manifest hash before using schema source. SQLite readonly connections close on success and error.

The scale origin check uses canonical recorded paths as metadata. It introduces no historical repository artifact dependency and retains the sparse-checkout input argument. Existing registered plans, all phases, budgets, 150 shards, 1500 samples, full parity and aggregate population are unchanged.
All fixed #159 private-target, actual-toolchain/fresh, exact semantic feature, Rust and previous source-guard changes remain byte-for-byte preserved.
limitations: Synthetic negative controls establish verifier behavior, not runtime performance or task completion.
Previously observed real artifacts keep the original source/schema/status; no original record has new producer fields backfilled.
Final executions must use the newly fixed source and its corresponding new evidence protocol.
scope: Minimal independently cross-reviewed adoption of nine validation paths from PR160 plus sparse checkout integration
